 Sandro Mamukelashvili chipped in 23 points (7-of-13 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists and one block over 32 minutes off the bench in Monday’s win over the Hawks.
 Mamukelashvili saw a massive uptick in minutes and offensive opportunities with Austin Reaves sitting out due to illness on the tail-end of a back-to-back for the Lakers. The 27-year-old drained 5-of-8 shots from three-point range and established season-high marks in both minutes and points. His fantasy appeal is strictly limited to situation-dependent matchups like this one where he receives extra chances.
 -  George Bissell

 Sandro Mamukelashvili (illness) is available for Friday’s game against the Trail Blazers. 
 Listed as questionable on the Lakers’ initial injury report, Mamu is good to go. He’ll take on his usual role as the first big off the Lakers’ bench. 
 Sandro Mamukelashvili 
 LAL 
 Forward-Center 
 #54 
 Sandro Mamukelashvili (illness) is questionable to play against the Trail Blazers on Friday. 
 Mamu has been a solid reserve for the Lakers this season and has yet to miss a game. His potential absence would likely open the door for both Jake LaRavia and Jarred Vanderbilt to take on more minutes. 
 Sandro Mamukelashvili 
 LAL 
 Forward-Center 
 #54 
 Sandro Mamukelashvili tallied 13 points (6-of-15 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers. 
 After totaling 21 points in the Lakers’ first three games, Mamukelashvili has hit double figures in each of his last two. Against the Clippers, his perimeter shot wasn’t falling, as he missed all five three-point attempts. But Mamu was 6-of-10 from two, and he did a little of everything else. Despite the bench role, Mamukelashvili is worth rostering in deep leagues. 
 Sandro Mamukelashvili 
 LAL 
 Forward-Center 
 #54 
 Sandro Mamukelashvili accounted for 17 points (6-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, one block and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 Mamu delivered excellent production off the bench for the Lakers in the first half of Tuesday’s game, scoring 13 points in 12 minutes. Unfortunately, he wasn’t as effective after halftime, scoring four points on 2-of-4 shooting. Although Tuesday was a tale of two halves for Mamukelashvili, his ability to score points in bunches makes the forward/center worth rostering in 14-team leagues. 
 Sandro Mamukelashvili 
 LAL 
 Forward-Center 
 #54 
 Sandro Mamukelashvili tallied 19 points (7-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Thursday’s exhibition against the Kings. 
 After scoring 15 points as a spot starter in Tuesday’s loss to the Warriors, Mamukelashvili returned to a reserve role on Thursday. He was excellent, shooting 70 percent from the field and putting up a complete stat line. While coming off the bench limits Mamukelashvili’s fantasy ceiling, his floor should be relatively safe because the Lakers need bench scoring. He’s worth considering in the late rounds of 12-team drafts. 
 Sandro Mamukelashvili 
 LAL 
 Forward-Center 
 #54 
 Sandro Mamukelashvili has agreed to a four-year, $52 million contract with the Lakers, reports ESPN’s Shams Charania. 
 Mamukelashvili had the best year of his career with the Raptors last yeah. The 27-year-old power forward averaged a career-high 11.2 points and shot 38 percent from behind the three-point line on a career-high 3.7 three-point attempts per game. Mamukelashvili finished 10th in the Sixth Man of the Year voting. He’ll continue to provide size and spacing as a role player with the Lakers. 
 Sandro Mamukelashvili 
 TOR 
 Forward-Center 
 #54 
 Sandro Mamukelashvili will decline his 2026-27 player option and become an unrestricted free agent. 
 Mamukelashvili, who would have made $2.8 million next season, stands to command a much better payday when free agency opens Tuesday night. Finishing tenth in NBA Sixth Man of the Year voting, the 6-foot-9 forward had the most productive season of his professional career. In 80 regular-season games, Mamukelashvili averaged 11.2 points, 4.9 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.4 three-pointers in 21.9 minutes, shooting 52.3 percent from the field and 74.7 percent from the foul line. Given the rumored market, Mamu may be able to find a more prominent role for himself, which would raise his fantasy ceiling. 
 Collin Murray-Boyles 
 TOR 
 Forward 
 #12 
 Collin Murray-Boyles recorded 17 points (6-of-10 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), seven rebounds, one assist, one steal and one blocked shot in Monday’s Game 2 loss to the Cavaliers. 
 Effective in 20 minutes in Game 1, Murray-Boyles played 26 minutes in Game 2. And the rookie replaced Jakob Poeltl (two points, four rebounds and one assist) in the lineup to begin the third quarter, with the veteran center not playing at all after halftime. While there is a need for Poeltl’s size, he was ineffective in Toronto’s first two games. We should see a lot more of Murray-Boyles and Sandro Mamukelashvili (12/10/2/1 with one three-pointer) in Thursday’s Game 3 as the Raptors look to avoid falling into a 0-3 hole.

 RJ Barrett put up 12 points (5-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, seven assists, two steals, and a block in loss on Wednesday to the Celtics. 
 RJ will have games where he will take a bunch of shots and miss a lot of them. The Raptors were without Kawhi Leonard and Scottie Barnes in this one, so the Raptors needed the offense.  Immanuel Quickley scored 11 points (3-of-14 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, a steal, and a three in 98-93 loss to the Celtics. 
 IQ was returning from a hamstring injury and this was his first game back. On the season, IQ has been shooting 38.7% from the field which is just not good enough. He’s a career 42.4% field goal shooter which should show that there is room for him to bounce back, but it’s undoubtedly been a slow start efficiency wise. The next opportunity to bounce back will be on Thursday against the Sixers.

 Ja’Kobe Walter scores 17 points (5-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, an assist, two steals, and five 3-pointers in the loss to the Celtics. 
 Walter got going early in the first quarter which helped the Raptors stay in the game in the first half. He led the team in scoring in this game which goes to show the offensive woes of the Raptors in this game. He also led the team in minutes with 35 of them. Overall, it was a bad game from the Raptors where they couldn’t even get offense from RJ Barrett. Solid game but Walter isn’t more than just a streamer.

 Neemias Queta with 11 points (2-of-4 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), 13 rebounds, three assists, a steal, three blocks, a three, and five turnovers against the Raptors. 
 Neemias Queta led the team with a +27 in this game which helps shows the impact he had on this game. He was active on defense and active on the boards. You don’t love the five turnovers, but the 30 minutes of play is very nice. He even hit a three which is something you don’t expect from him.
